projects.title: Mobile Game Design Project
projects.description:
This project was to create Android powered mobile games, combining the disciplines of Computer Science with Graphic Design.  The project was organized into three teams to create their own games.  The teams consisted of a developer paired with a graphic designer who then spent the entire quarter working on planning, designing, testing, and playing their creations.  The project culminated in a launch party where the 5 designed games were on display to the public and presentations about the design process of each game were given.

For the developers: Students used libGDX to build their games combined with Android SDKs to test on mobile devices. The target environment was Android 4.0+.

For the graphic designers: Students used Photoshop to create their assets.

projects.title: Senior Capstone Project
projects.description:
For this project, the 2013 Senior Capstone class worked with three NAO robots (http://www.aldebaran-robotics.com/en/) to make a presentation in which the robots gave most of the presentation. Various examples of things we did was make the robots greet the audience as members walked in, speak about themselves, and perform demonstrations of their capabilities in games such as Tic-Tac-Toe and Copycat.

The class was split into three teams: coding, documentation, and testing. In particular, I was the manager of the coding group. I was in charge of dividing work among my 9 team members so that everyone had sufficient work to do and all the required tasks were achieved. I assisted the project in various ways such as stress testing the robot's battery life, recording hours worked for my team, dealing with inter-team communication issues, and giving feedback to the work done by the documentation and testing teams.
